topic.title: Conditional utility of task-mask membership
topic.question: Under the frozen inputs, history policy and training protocol, does task-mask membership improve click AUC beyond aligned historical item content and action codes in the strongest visible model, at justified parameter and measured runtime cost?
topic.hypothesis: Task-mask membership may supply useful event assignment beyond item content and historical actions; the compact evidence does not establish this. Inherit the strongest visible trial unchanged as the utility control. Compare full membership use with a membership-blind representation and a counts-only replacement to distinguish event assignment from task-history frequency. Keep host mask construction, valid history, event order, aligned item fields and actions, target inputs, supervision and training exposure fixed; representation controls must not expose padded events or alter label construction. Use matched-capacity replacements and measure training and inference cost. A valid-history membership-permutation control should preserve per-task counts and joint membership patterns while disrupting their association with event content. Full membership failing to beat these controls would undermine its conditional utility; an apparent gain explained by capacity, cost or frequency would not establish useful event assignment. Repeat a discriminating comparison before claiming support, reserving resources for attribution and assessment. This question concerns representation use of masks, distinct from changing historical actions or auxiliary-gradient participation.
